history.dynasty: Portuguese-era (1818); built by the Saraswat Brahmin community with local Hindu devotees
history.summary: Shree Mahalaxmi Temple on Dr Dada Vaidya Road, Panaji, is dedicated to Goddess Mahalakshmi, the presiding deity of Panaji, and is described as the first Hindu temple permitted to be built in Portuguese Goa after nearly 300 years. Its history: in the 16th century Havig (Havika) Brahmins from Karwar-Kumtha carried the deity's image to Taleigao in Goa; fearing Portuguese persecution they moved it to Mayem village in Bicholim, where it remained till 1817. Narayan Kamat Mhamai of Panaji then brought it back, and the liberal Portuguese governor Conde de Rio Pardo granted permission to build on 2 July 1818; the deity was consecrated and the foundation stone laid on 10 July 1818, with the temple completed by 1819 (official history, goa.gov.in). The original marble deity is said to lie in a small box in the rear wall behind the present main idol. The temple was renovated in 1983. The deity is described as a peaceful four-armed form wearing a linga on her head. Coordinates are approximate (city-level, verify).

town_description: Panaji (Panjim) is the capital city of Goa, set on the southern bank of the Mandovi River estuary in North Goa district. It became the Portuguese capital of Goa in 1843 and retains a colonial character in its Latin Quarter of Fontainhas, while Altinho Hill hosts the archbishop's palace and state government buildings. It is the state's administrative and cultural centre and the main gateway for North Goa tourism.

travel.road: On Dr Dada Vaidya Road in central Panaji; NH-66 passes through the city; KTC intercity and local buses available (verify)
